ApplicantDhanashwari Devi has filed the present application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the 'Cr.PC'), Whether Reporters of local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
for releasing her on bail, during the pendency of the trial, in case FIR No.61 of 2023, dated 28.05.2023, registered .
under Sections 306, 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as the 'IPC'), registered with Police Station Dhanotu, District Mandi, H.P. of 2.
According to the applicant, she is an innocent person and having no criminal history.
rt 3. The applicant is in judicial custody, as such, it has been pleaded that she is no longer required by the Police, as she is innocent person.
4. According to the applicant, she has no concern, whatsoever, with the offence, in which, she has been arrested by the Police.
5. In the application, certain undertakings have been given, on behalf of the applicant, for which, she is ready to abide by, in case, she is released on bail, during the pendency of the trial.

sentences.text:
The applicant has also tried her luck by moving the application under Section 439 Cr.P.C., before the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Sundernagar, however, her bail application bearing No.171 of 2023, has been dismissed vide order dated 15.07.2023.
.
7.

When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein, the fact that the FIR,
in question, has been registered on the basis of the statement of complainant Saroj Kumari,
recorded under of Section 154 Cr.PC.
She has mentioned that they are five sisters and one brother.
Parents of the complainant are no more in the land of living.
Her sister Tanuja, had married with Vikrant son of the applicant, about two years ago.
7.2. After 15 days of the marriage, brotherinlaw of the complainant, Vikrant has started beating her.
The motherinlaw and brotherinlaw of the sister of the complainant also used to mentally torture her and abuse her.
7.3. In the year 2022, her sister Tanuja had also lodged a complaint against the applicant and her son Ravikant for torturing her physically and mentally.
All the three accused used to beat her and torture her.

7.4. On 28.5.2023, at about 8.30 a.m., sister of the complainant informed her that Tanuja has been beaten by .
her husband and she has also forwarded the photographs of Tanuja on Whatsapp, in which, blood is seen on the mouth of Tanuja.
After sometime, Police informed that Tanuja had committed suicide by hanging.
Lastly, she has complained that her sister had taken the extreme step on account of physical and mental rt torture and beatings given to her by her inlaws.
8. On the basis of the above facts, the police registered the FIR, in question, and the police machinery swung into motion.
9. During investigation, the spot was visited.
The team from RFSL also visited the spot and collected, all the physical evidence.
The dead body of Tanuja was sent for postmortem examination.
10. It is the further case of the police that on 28.5.2023, an altercation took place between deceased Tanuja with accused Vikrant.
On 28.5.2023, all the three accused were arrested.
11. As per the status report, against the applicant, FIR No.19/10, dated 07.01.2010, under Sections 451, 323, .

sentences.text: It has also been found that on 27.6.2022, deceased had lodged a complaint against the accused rt persons, upon which, the proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act, were initiated.
13. The mobile phones, allegedly used by the accused persons, have been sent to SFSL, Junga for retrieving the deleted data.
14. On the basis of the stand taken in the status report, a prayer has been made to dismiss the application.

15. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the applicant has also placed on record a certificate issued by MHC, Police Station, Dhanotu, in which, the factum of acquittal of the applicant, in the above noted two cases, has been mentioned.
16.

The role allegedly played by the applicant, in the commission of the crime, will be proved during the .
trial, when the police will file the final report under Section 173(2) Cr.PC.
17.

The applicant is in judicial custody and no useful purpose would be served by keeping her in judicial of custody for indefinite period, as the chances of commencement and conclusion of the trial, against the rt applicant, in near future, are not so bright.

18. Applicant is permanent resident of District Mandi and no apprehension has been expressed by the police that, in case, the applicant is ordered to be released, on bail, she may coerce the witnesses,
not to depose against her, or she may not be available for the trial.
19. The applicant has asserted her age as 55 years.
No doubt, a valuable human life has been lost, but merely, on this ground, the application cannot be rejected as a matter of punishment, as pretrial punishment is prohibited under the law.

Moreover,
the presumption of innocence is still in favour of accused (applicant).
20.

Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the bail application is liable to be .
allowed and is accordingly allowed.

21. The applicant is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No.61 of 2023, dated 28.05.2023,
under Sections 306, 498A read with Section 34 IPC, of registered with Police Station, Dhanotu,
District Mandi, H.P., on her furnishing personal bond in the sum of rt Rs.50,000/, with one surety in the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions, Sundernagar, District Mandi,
H.P.

sentences.text: 20. Any of the observations made herein above shall of not be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case, as, these observations are confined only to the rt disposal of the present bail application.
21. It is made clear that the respondentState is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions is found to be violated by the applicant/petitioner.

22. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of the concerned jail, through email, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the eprison software.

23. In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent of the concerned jail is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary of the concerned DLSA.
The Superintendent of the concerned jail, is further directed that if the applicant fails to furnish the bail bonds, as per the order passed by this Court, within a period of one .
month from today
, then, the said fact be submitted to this Court.
